summary: A compact architectural stop in Bangkok’s old town: Loha Prasat rises through tiers of golden metal spires, with a central staircase, Buddhist interpretation and elevated neighbourhood views. Shortlist it if distinctive buildings and a quiet, self-paced temple visit appeal. It combines naturally with the Golden Mount rather than requiring a dedicated half-day.
whyGo: See the striking geometry of 37 spires, representing Buddhist practices toward enlightenment.
Explore exhibition areas and climb through the structure toward the relic shrine and city views.
Enjoy an architectural contrast with Bangkok’s more familiar temple halls and riverside monuments.
bestFor: Travellers seeking a short cultural stop
skipIf: Stair climbing is difficult and the upper-level experience is your main reason to visit
You are already tired of temples and need an interactive activity
duration: Allow 45–60 minutes as a planning estimate, longer for photography or reading displays.
cost: Bangkok municipal visitor material lists THB 20 for foreigners and free admission for Thai visitors. That material is older; confirm the current Loha Prasat charge locally and carry small cash.
hours: TAT’s Japan office lists daily 09:00–17:00. Older municipal material lists 08:00–17:00; use 09:00–16:00 as a conservative arrival window and verify before making a special journey.
bestTime: Morning for a less hot walk; mid-afternoon for photographs while still allowing time before closure.
gettingThere: Thanon Maha Chai, Phra Nakhon. TAT lists a roughly 15-minute walk from MRT Sam Yot (BL30). A taxi can reduce walking; allow for old-town traffic.
booking: No advance reservation requirement was found for ordinary visits. Check local access arrangements around religious ceremonies; TAT lists telephone 02-224-8807.
accessibility: Upper floors require stairs, including the central staircase. Step-free access, accessible toilets and lift availability were not established; mobility-limited visitors should confirm directly before travelling.
practicalTips: Wear temple-appropriate clothing covering shoulders and knees; follow shoe-removal signs.
Carry water and sun protection for the approach and exposed grounds.
Treat shrine areas as active religious spaces; keep voices low and follow photography signs.
The included 2018 photograph shows the golden-spire appearance; much older online photos show dark spires.
decemberNotes: A flexible December daytime stop with no date-specific booking identified. Leave room for shade breaks even in the cooler season. No December 2026 ceremony calendar or special closure schedule was verified; do not assume evening interior access from illuminated exterior photographs.
uncertainties: Current admission price and final admission time remain unconfirmed by the temple.
Official tourism publications disagree on opening time.
Accessible facilities and December 2026 special closures are unknown.
